correctness.rationale: The stated law is correct. After a first vertex a_i, either a second A vertex takes color 1 before b_i, forcing a two-color side partition, or b_i closes a paired color 1 (probability 1/n). At least two interposed B vertices force exactly three colors. Zero or one interposed vertex has combined probability 3/[2(2n-1)] and gives one plus the smaller crown color count. The frozen proof's literal uniform-order assertion for one interposed vertex is false: the induced order is uniform conditional on starting on side B. The side-exchange automorphism gives precisely the same color-count distribution conditional on either starting side, so it justifies the recurrence without changing the claim. The n=2 base is two disjoint edges; maximum degree yields the bound n. The factorial expression follows by splitting odd/even factors; the tail ratio is at most 2/7 for the relevant m=n-k+3≥4, bounding the remainder after the first two terms. Independent direct permutation counts for n=2,3,4,5 agreed, including (2903040,574560,108000,43200) for colors 2 through 5 at n=5. Replay: /workspace/branches/b72df666-d704-4f8f-b5e8-83e6f97d7207/direct_crown_check.py and direct_crown_check.log. The frozen memoized n≤7 output was inspected, not executed; bounded checks do not certify the infinite law.
